name: Gallery Koyanagi
about_text: Gallery Koyanagi is a contemporary art gallery in Tokyo's Ginza district, occupying the ninth floor of the Koyanagi Building. It represents a roster of Japanese and international artists working across photography, sculpture, painting, video, and installation, including Hiroshi Sugimoto, Yoshihiro Suda, Christian Marclay, Marlene Dumas, and Tabaimo. The gallery's history is tied to Toho Koyanagi (Koyanagi Ceramics), a predecessor referenced in artist research on the space's Ginza site. Its program spans emerging and established artists, with regular solo and group exhibitions, museum collaborations, and participation in Art Week Tokyo. The gallery has also produced limited-edition publications and supported artists' museum surveys internationally, reflecting a program oriented toward serious, research-driven contemporary practice rather than purely market-driven display.

kind_evidence: Site presents a roster of represented artists with individual artist pages, gallery exhibitions, and art fair participation (Art Week Tokyo).
notes: Contact page lists gallery hours and location in both English and Japanese; news page documents extensive museum and institutional exhibition history for represented artists, but no direct statement of the gallery's own founding date or founders.

triage.site_notes: Bilingual (jp/en) WordPress-style site organized by CMS post types (exhibition, news, interview, event) with no clear consolidated exhibitions archive list; each exhibition, artist, and work has its own permalink, and roster is accessible via /jp/artists and /en/artists index pages. The site organises content by individual exhibition pages (JP and EN, numbered slugs like e24, 44-2) rather than a consolidated archive list, plus per-artwork 'work' pages and dated 'news' posts; no roster index, about, or contact page appeared in this batch, so these were added to fetch_more as they are almost certainly linked from top navigation. The crawled sample is dominated by individual exhibition pages (both Japanese /exhibitions/ and English /en/exhibitions/ URLs, largely duplicate content) and individual artwork pages under /work/, with no roster index, about, or contact page appearing in this slice; the site likely has separate top-level pages for these that were not captured in the sample.
